claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The paper states that large-scale studies find autonomous coding agents' pull requests are produced faster but accepted less often, a coordination and trust gap that PR-level telemetry cannot explain.
claims.quote: Autonomous coding agents now open millions of pull requests, yet large-scale studies find their PRs are produced faster but accepted less often - a coordination and trust gap that pull-request-level telemetry cannot explain.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Using the grite coordination substrate, the share of work that merely re-does a teammate's task fell from 78% to 0% while useful throughput more than tripled, at bounded overhead.
claims.quote: We show that (i) this shared substrate reduces duplicate and conflicting work at bounded overhead - the share of work that merely re-does a teammate's task falls from 78% to 0% while useful throughput more than triples;

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Every agent's copy of the grite event log converges to the same state with no write silently dropped, whereas a file-based tracker loses concurrent writes.
claims.quote: (ii) every agent's copy of the log converges to the same state with no write silently dropped, where a file-based tracker loses concurrent writes;

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: grite is an open-source coordination substrate requiring no central server, storing append-only signed event records inside git itself so the coordination process is captured directly.
claims.quote: We study this process through grite, our open-source coordination substrate that needs no central server and stores its records inside git itself, so its append-only, signed event log captures the coordination process directly.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The coordination log is a mineable artefact from which failure modes such as conflicting edits, lock starvation, redundant rediscovery and race-to-close are recoverable with provenance, several of them invisible in pull-request history.
claims.quote: (iii) the log is a mineable artefact from which concrete failure modes - conflicting edits, lock starvation, redundant rediscovery, race-to-close - are automatically recoverable with provenance, several invisible in pull-request history.
